_comment: Voice-over script for the SystemOverview composition. `at` is the scene start in seconds at 30fps; `budget` is how long that scene runs. Keep each line comfortably under its budget at ~2.5 words/second.

lines.text: A cement plant runs on 133 machines. Every one needs inspecting.
This is CPIIS, the system I built to make that happen.
Most plants still run inspections on paper. The data gets collected, then thrown away.
It starts with the plant itself. Areas, sections, equipment, and the individual parts an inspector actually touches.
You write a checklist once. The system turns it into recurring tasks, spread evenly across the Sunday to Thursday work week.
The engineer works from a phone on the plant floor. Forty two checkpoints, condition, notes, and photo evidence.
Anything wrong becomes a finding, and every finding becomes a maintenance action with a severity, an owner and a due date.
Managers get four dashboards. Schedule compliance, inspection coverage, mean time to repair, backlog aging, and risk weighted by criticality.
Plus a daily report that builds its own PDF and emails itself to the right people.
Access is a live matrix. Eleven roles, eight permissions, enforced inside the database, not just hidden in the interface.
So the whole loop closes. Sign up, get approved, inspect, raise a finding, close the action, and watch the numbers move.
Built on Next.js, React and Supabase, with row level security in Postgres.
CPIIS. Inspection, findings, maintenance and reporting, end to end.
